questions.prompt: In File Upload Fundamentals, which statement best describes Multipart form data?
options: Treat filenames, MIME types and file contents as untrusted. Limit request size, generate storage names, constrain resolved paths, and keep private objects outside a public static directory.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Choose a parser that matches the request Content-Type and apply a size limit. Parsing produces values; it does not establish that those values are safe or satisfy the application schema.
questions.answer_key: Choose a parser that matches the request Content-Type and apply a size limit. Parsing produces values; it does not establish that those values are safe or satisfy the application schema.
questions.explanation: Choose a parser that matches the request Content-Type and apply a size limit. Parsing produces values; it does not establish that those values are safe or satisfy the application schema.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying File Upload Fundamentals?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
Uploads, API calls, and webhooks cross trust boundaries. Limit file sizes, verify content and signatures, use timeouts, retry only safe operations, and make duplicate webhook delivery idempotent.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Uploads, API calls, and webhooks cross trust boundaries. Limit file sizes, verify content and signatures, use timeouts, retry only safe operations, and make duplicate webhook delivery idempotent.
questions.explanation: Uploads, API calls, and webhooks cross trust boundaries. Limit file sizes, verify content and signatures, use timeouts, retry only safe operations, and make duplicate webhook delivery idempotent.

questions.prompt: A change related to File Upload Fundamentals appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
